**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Some tests require to know what IP family are they testing in order to work for both IPv4 and IPv6 families.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #78099 
Fixes #80388

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

Adding an option to the test context is the simpler way to provide this information to all the tests.
This PR autodetect the cluster (primary in case of dual stack) IP family based on the ClusterIP of the kubernetes service created in the default namespace.The clusterIP is single stack always.

```
kubectl get services --all-namespaces
NAMESPACE     NAME         TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)                  AGE
default       kubernetes   ClusterIP   fd00:10:96::1   <none>        443/TCP                  28m
```
Current mechanism doesn´t detect dual-stack cluster because there is  no needed at this moment

> Adding an option to the test context is the simpler way to provide this information to all the tests.
We can iterate over this and provide an autodetecting mechanism, but this is the simpler way and allows to unblock the work to add IPv6 support to all the e2e tests

why not add the auto-detecting utility and use it in tests that need it?
i think over time, the context of the framework became a location that holds "all the things", which is quite bad.

also, flags/fields added on the e2e-testing framework propagate in user setups and test-infra jobs and are difficult to deprecate.

per discussion, https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C9NK9KFFW/p1563828920018000 is better to avoid flags and use autodetection

issue_context.title: E2Es for hostport/HostIP resolution to conformance does not support IPv6
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting reports about failing tests in Kubernetes CI jobs -->

**Which jobs are failing**:

https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/conformance-all#kind%20(IPv6),%20master%20(dev)

**Which test(s) are failing**:

[sig-scheduling] SchedulerPredicates [Serial] validates that there is no conflict between pods with same hostPort but different hostIP and protocol [Conformance]

**Since when has it been failing**:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/78350

**Testgrid link**:

https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/conformance-all#kind%20(IPv6),%20master%20(dev)

**Reason for failure**:

The tests checks for 0.0.0.0 that is IPv4 only

**Anything else we need to know**:

Probably I should check with SIG-Testing how can we add an ipv6 job and update the KEP accordingly https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1139 

EDIT
Probably I should check with SIG-Testing how can we add an ipv6 job as part of the k/k presubmits, and update the KEP accordingly https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1139  😅

review_comments:
/hold 

IMO we need to have auto-detection for this type of behavior. 

/assign @timothysc.
@timothysc I've added the variable here so is available to all the tests, but it's populated using a detection function at the beginning of the testing, in `test/e2e/e2e.go`, I've removed the flag

there is so much random stuff in the context and that's a prime example of organic growth.

seems to me we should not add more fields to the context or flags to the CLI, or at least that's what i understood was the plan. it might slightly increase the test suite runtime if the detection func  is called multiple times, but it still feels better.

I didn't know how to make this variable available to all the tests, would be happy to change it if you give me some advice.
 I don't think that running the function multiple times is a good option, at least without caching, since the IP family of the cluster is immutable.

> I didn't know how to make this variable available to all the tests, would be happy to change it if you give me some advice.

the context is the dumping ground for all shared fields, which wrong. but AFAIK there is no other way to share properties right now.

> I don't think that running the function multiple times is a good option, at least without caching, since the IP family of the cluster is immutable.

in my view the API call should be pretty cheap, but yes if the `kubernetes` service is not changing it's IP family then it is a bit of a waste. i'd still go calling it multiple times and not depending on the context though.

/assign @oomichi 
^ for opinion here too.

Sorry for my late response.
The cost of the API call `c.CoreV1().Services(metav1.NamespaceDefault).Get("kubernetes", metav1.GetOptions{})` can be cheap then it doesn't matter if we don't use cache here.
I saw @neolit123's point because I am not sure the string `ipv4` / `ipv6` could be nice for the global context for the code readability.
How about adding comment at least like
```
	// The IP Family of the cluster ("ipv4" or "ipv6")
	IPFamily string
```
even if not changing the code?

I was going to use without `0::`, but wanted to keep it consistent with the rfc https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2765
> 2.1.  Addresses

   In addition to the forms of addresses defined in [ADDR-ARCH] this
   document also introduces the new form of IPv4-translated address.
   This is needed to avoid using IPv4-compatible addresses outside the
   intended use of automatic tunneling.  Thus the address forms are:

         IPv4-mapped:
                 An address of the form 0::ffff:a.b.c.d which refers
                 to a node that is not IPv6-capable. 


I think it´s cosmetic, both representations are equivalent AFAIK

This is a bit weird IMO, we're determining IP family by checking the cluster IP but we are validating host IP with it. Can we confirm that the host IP is always matching whatever the primary cluster IP is?

the problem with these tests are they are using hardcoded IPv4 addresses.
The `TranslateIPv4ToIPv6(hostIP)` function returns the hostIP as IPv6, only if the cluster family is IPv6, otherwise returns hostIP without any change (as an IPv4 address)
But this would break if an e2e test ends up passing in a v6 address for hostIP here right? We should account for that here or at the very least document that.

ahh, ok got it, you are right, I was only focused on these tests since `createHostPortonNode` is not exported but I think I can modify the TranslateIPv4ToIPv6 to verify that the IP passed as argument is IPv4, otherwise do nothing
